text:
Livewire 4.1 introduced notable modifications to how `wire:model` and its associated modifiers function, primarily impacting data synchronization and event propagation. These updates aim to offer developers more precise control over client-side behavior and network requests. ## Refined Control Over Client-Side State Synchronization In Livewire 4.1, modifiers such as `.blur`, `.change`, and `.enter` now govern not only when network requests are sent but also when the client-side state (`$wire.property`) is synchronized [1][2]. This is a significant shift from previous versions, where client-side updates occurred immediately as a user typed, while these modifiers only affected the timing of network requests. To revert to the previous behavior—where the client-side state updates immediately, and the modifier only dictates network timing—the `.live` modifier must now be prepended. For example, `wire:model.blur` in Livewire 4.1 will delay both client-side and server-side updates until the input loses focus. To achieve the Livewire 3 behavior (immediate client-side update, server update on blur), developers must use `wire:model.live.blur` [1][2]. Similarly, `wire:model.live.change` and `wire:model.live.enter` restore the previous network timing for their respective events [3]. ## Adjusted Event Listening for Nested Elements Livewire 4.x altered the default event propagation behavior for `wire:model`. Previously, in Livewire 3, `wire:model` would implicitly listen for input/change events that bubbled up from child elements [4][2]. This could lead to unexpected interactions, such as a modal closing if an input within it triggered a bubbling change event. In Livewire 4.1, `wire:model` by default only listens for events originating directly on the element it is bound to [2]. To enable `wire:model` to capture events that bubble up from child elements, the **`.deep`** modifier must be explicitly added (e.g., `
`) [1][3]. This change enhances predictability by requiring developers to opt-in to listening for child events. ## Specific Modifier Interactions and Bug Fixes Livewire 4.1.0 initially contained a bug where `wire:model.blur` did not send the input's value in the payload when a form was submitted by pressing the Enter key from that input [5]. This issue, which could lead to lost user data, was quickly resolved in Livewire 4.1.1 [5]. Additionally, the `.blur` modifier does not function as expected with `Modelable` components. This is because blur events do not propagate from inner inputs to the component's root element, making it impossible for the parent component to capture them. For `Modelable` components, modifiers that control network timing, such as `wire:model` (deferred sync) or `wire:model.live` (immediate network request), are supported on the component itself. Any input-level timing, like `.blur`, should be handled within the child component's own internal `wire:model` bindings [6]. Other modifiers, such as `.number` and `.boolean` for type casting, and `.renderless` for skipping component re-renders, continue to function as described in Livewire 4.x documentation [3][7]. These changes in Livewire 4.1 provide greater control over data binding and event handling, necessitating that developers review and potentially adapt their existing `wire:model` implementations to align with the new, more explicit behaviors.

sources.title: Upgrade Guide | Laravel Livewire
claims: In Livewire v4.1, modifiers like .blur and .change now control when client-side state syncs, not just network timing.
If using .blur or .change modifiers in Livewire v4.1 and wanting the previous behavior, add .live before them (e.g., wire:model.live.blur).
In Livewire v4, wire:model now only listens for events originating directly on the element itself (equivalent to the .self modifier behavior).
In Livewire v4, to capture events from child elements with wire:model, add the .deep modifier (e.g., wire:model.deep="value").
In Livewire v4, wire:model expressions now support bracket notation for accessing nested properties (e.g., wire:model="foo['bar']['baz']" or wire:model="items[0].name").
In Livewire v4, the $wire.$js() method for defining JavaScript actions has been deprecated.
In Livewire v4, the use of $js in scripts without $wire.$js or this.$js prefix has been deprecated.
In Livewire v4, the commit and request hooks have been deprecated in favor of a new interceptor system.
In Livewire v4, the $errors magic property can be used to access a component's error bag from JavaScript.
In Livewire v4, the $intercept magic property can be used to intercept and modify Livewire requests from JavaScript.

sources.title: wire:model | Laravel Livewire
claims: The `.live` modifier for `wire:model` sends property updates to the server as a user types into an input field.
When using `wire:model.live`, Livewire adds a 150-millisecond debounce to server updates by default.
The debounce timing for `wire:model.live` can be customized using `.debounce.Xms`, for example, `.debounce.250ms`.
The `.blur` modifier for `wire:model` delays syncing until the user clicks away from the input.
The `.change` modifier for `wire:model` triggers on the change event, useful for select elements.
The `.enter` modifier for `wire:model` syncs when the user presses the Enter key.
The `.deep` modifier for `wire:model` makes it listen to events bubbling up from child elements.
The `.renderless` modifier for `wire:model` sends a live model update to the server without re-rendering the component.
The `.number` modifier for `wire:model` casts the value to an integer on the server.
The `.boolean` modifier for `wire:model` casts the value to a boolean on the server.

sources.title: Migration Guide | livewire/livewire | DeepWiki
claims: In Livewire V3, `wire:model` responded to events bubbling from child elements, while V4 changes this to only respond to events on the element itself.
To restore V3 behavior for `wire:model` event bubbling in V4, the `.bubble` modifier must be added.
In Livewire V3, `wire:scroll` was used for preserving scroll position in persisted containers, whereas V4 requires `wire:navigate:scroll`.
Livewire V3 `wire:transition` used Alpine's `x-transition` with modifiers, but V4 uses the native View Transitions API, removing all transition modifiers.

In Livewire V3, JavaScript actions were handled differently than in V4, where deprecated APIs like `Livewire.hook('commit', ...)` are replaced by `Livewire.interceptMessage(...)` and `Livewire.hook('request', ...)` is replaced by `Livewire.interceptRequest(...)`.
The `stream()` method parameter order changed from V3 to V4, with `content` now coming first and the `to` parameter being renamed to `el`.

Livewire V4's single-file components use the same syntax as Volt class-based components, allowing for migration by updating component imports, removing the Volt service provider, uninstalling Volt, and installing Livewire v4.
Livewire V4 introduces automatic performance enhancements, including non-blocking operations for `wire:poll` and parallel execution for `wire:model.live` requests.
Livewire V4 consolidates array/object updates to reduce redundant processing, which may require code adjustments if individual index hooks were relied upon for replacing entire arrays.
To upgrade to Livewire V4, prerequisites include backing up the application and database, reviewing breaking changes, and ensuring compatibility with Laravel version 10+ and PHP version 8.1+.

sources.title: v4.1 wire:model.blur not sending input's values w/ payload when Enter pressed in same input to submit form · livewire/livewire · Discussion #9858 · GitHub
claims: In Livewire v4.1.0, the `wire:model.blur` modifier does not send the input's value in the payload when the Enter key is pressed to submit a form from that input, unless the `.enter` modifier is also added.
The issue was reported by jeffchown on January 28, 2026.
A fix for the issue was submitted by joshhanley via PR #9873 on January 30, 2026.
The fix was confirmed to work by jeffchown after updating to Livewire v4.1.1 on February 3, 2026.

sources.title: wire:model modifiers bug with Modelable components · livewire/livewire · Discussion #9952 · GitHub
claims: The `wire:model.blur` modifier does not work as expected on modelable Livewire components.
The `wire:model.live.blur` modifier does not send a network request on blur for modelable components.
The `wire:model.blur.live` modifier updates local state and sends a network request on every input event for modelable components.
The `.blur` modifier is not supported on modelable child components because blur events do not bubble up from inner inputs to the component root.
Modifiers that are meaningful on a modelable component relate to network timing: `wire:model` (deferred sync) and `wire:model.live` (sends network request on value change).
Input-level timing for modelable components should be controlled by the child component's own inner `wire:model` binding, e.g., `<flux:input wire:model.blur="value" />`.
The Livewire version used in the discussion was v4.1.3.
The Laravel version used in the discussion was v12.50.0.
The PHP version used in the discussion was 8.4.

claims: The `.live` modifier for `wire:model` sends property updates to the server as a user types.
By default, `wire:model.live` has a 150-millisecond debounce.
The debounce time for `wire:model.live` can be customized using `.debounce.Xms`, for example, `.debounce.250ms`.
The `.blur` modifier for `wire:model` delays syncing until the user clicks away from the input.
The `.change` modifier for `wire:model` triggers on the change event, useful for select elements.
The `.enter` modifier for `wire:model` syncs when the user presses the Enter key.
The `.deep` modifier for `wire:model` makes it listen to events bubbling up from child elements.
`wire:model` supports dot notation for binding to nested properties, array elements, and form object fields, e.g., `wire:model="address.city"`.
Bracket notation is supported as an alternative to dot notation, e.g., `wire:model="address\[\'city\']"`.
The `.renderless` modifier for `wire:model` sends a live model update to the server without re-rendering the component.
